LLM_description:
Situation:
A severe storm surge and flooding event has disrupted ground lines of communication across the central corridor. Supply Depot Alpha (northern airhead) and Supply Depot Bravo (coastal port) remain operational with constrained, day-by-day availability. Priority receiving elements include the 3rd Relief Battalion (Sector East), Field Hospital Charlie (Urban Core), Urban Distribution Company Delta (River District), and Shelter Support Group Echo (Highlands IDP sites). Road conditions are degraded; the riverside axis is intermittently inundated, the ridge route is passable but landslide-prone, and inner-city approaches require security escort. We will move mixed loads of food and medical supplies; supply volumes and packaging drive vehicle space requirements.

Mission:
Deliver essential supplies from the depots to the designated units across the current operational period to meet life-sustaining needs while minimizing total operational cost, comprising per-unit transport costs, fixed route security risk costs, vehicle deployment costs, and penalties for any authorized shortfalls.

Execution/Concept:
- Flows originate from authorized depots and must not exceed on-hand stocks by supply type and day. Unit-level daily demands must be met; controlled shortfalls are permitted only where operationally justified and will incur penalty costs reflecting humanitarian impact.
- Vehicle load plans must respect capacity limits. The required vehicle count on each origin–destination axis is driven by supply volumes and the capacity of the assigned vehicles. Fleet allocation is recalculated each day and cannot exceed the total available fleet.
- Route activation is controlled at the origin–destination–day level. Activating any route on a given day (dispatching one or more vehicles) triggers a fixed Risk Cost to cover escorts, route clearance/EOD, and command-and-control overhead. This Risk Cost is incurred once per activated route-day, regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched on that route.
- Transport costs vary by origin–destination and supply type. Vehicle deployment carries a per-vehicle cost. Where access is constrained or risk overhead dominates, consolidate loads on fewer activated routes while ensuring priority deliveries (e.g., time-sensitive medical cargo) are protected.
- Planning priorities: secure the minimum lifesaving package to Field Hospital Charlie and the 3rd Relief Battalion first, then expand to broader distribution nodes. Maintain flexibility to shift flows if a corridor degrades. Avoid activating marginal routes unless required to avert high penalties for critical shortfalls.
